expectations.text: The survey evidence is used to justify the audience-presence score but is not allowed to override the funding floor.
expectations.evidence: Section 3 ties the survey directly and only to the scoring: "Podcast's value-5 on audience presence and reachability is direct evidence: 200-signup survey, top answer, buyer named the exact 2–3 shows." The starved-family promotion is gated on four conditions where evidence is just one, and the floor is a separate, independently-checked condition: "(3) budget clears the family's floor *by concentrating on known-good shows* (math below)". Section 5 then enforces the floor rather than letting evidence waive it: "Start with one show, not two or three at once", a full-quarter flight at ~$5,000–7,50

expectations.evidence: The transcript does use the survey as audience evidence for show selection and explicitly privileges it there: 'You have real data I don't: the 2–3 shows your 200 survey respondents actually named. Use those as the anchor picks — survey data beats my guesswork every time,' and 'cross-check against what your survey turned up.' It separately states an economic floor: '$9K/month needs roughly 88 new paying customers/month to be self-funding purely from this channel.
